I've seen pages like this one that tell you how congressmen voted on a specific occasion, but I have no idea how to find pages like that.

For example, I was curious to know how the votes fell on the DMCA when it was first passed in 1998. There are a few links on the Wikipedia page but after poking around a bit I haven't found anything like the roll call linked above, and I can't determine how a specific congressman, such as Bernie Sanders, voted. Does anyone know a general way of finding out how people voted on a certain law? Seems like something I ought to be able to find out.
How can I determine who voted for a law?
I Googled "Digital Millenium Copyright Act vote record." This site popped up. If you scroll down to history, you can see a link to the voting record.

here's one way:

  • go to https://www.congress.gov/
  • find the search bar at the top.
  • for a useful (and interesting?) example, type "affordable care act", then when it shows you the results for the current Congress, find the box on the left where you can find results for past sessions. select the 111th Congress.
  • the top result should now be the Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act, more often called Obamacare. click the 'H.R. 3590' link.
  • click the 'Actions' tab.
  • on 3/21/2010 the House passed the conference report; click the 'Roll no. 165' link.
  • you have a list like the one you posted!

(see my follow up comment for some words of caution in finding and interpreting this sort of result.)

note a few challenges you'll encounter if you do this a lot:

  • there are MANY more bills proposed than laws passed. thus, many of the search results don't have any roll call votes associated with them, and you won't find a convenient report of which legislators support(ed) the bill.
  • there are usually many versions of a popular bill idea; there were probably dozens (or more) public health care bills proposed during every session of Congress between the late 1950s and the 2009-2010 session, when the ACA was passed. looking at the wrong one - one that wasn't passed - can be confusing.
  • the congressional actions taken on bills, and particularly passed laws, are often very complex. the ACA started as a totally unrelated bill - you can see it was passed unanimously in October 2009, and we can be sure it wasn't the ACA when that happened - and only as of the Senate vote (see that Actions list again) was it largely the law we know now. so, one has to be certain she's looking at the right vote in order to interpret the roll call record.

happy searching - and careful interpretation!
Thanks that's a big help. I will also look at govtrack.us but it's good to have a way to do it from a .gov site.

The recent debate about the Confederate flag has been making its circles in conspiracy communities as well as in libertarian and other "states rights" friendly communities.

I've been meaning to make a statement about this thing but something just kept nagging at me that wouldn't allow me to outright support state's rights by virtue of supporting the Confederate Battle flag.

I support state's rights 100% and without question, I feel as though the federal government has failed to competently fulfill its own constitutional role such as minting currency and collecting taxes in a lawful way.

That being said and the reason I have never flown a Confederate flag, the flag represents much more than state's rights. Even if that is the only thing it means to you, you are allowing those who oppose state's rights to control the debate under the context of all those other things the Confederate flag might represent to individuals across the country.

Pride in your heritage is great and dandy but that heritage happened in the past and its there, it can't be taken away from you. You don't have to fight for your heritage because you're born with it, all you have to do is embrace it or reject it.

State's rights on the other hand need to be fought for, they can be (and have been) taken away.

The state's rights movement and supporters need to rally around a new flag. We need a flag that doesn't have the bagadge of slavery and civil war. We need a flag that everyone who believes in state's rights can fly without having to ignore the "other things" that flag might represent to our neighbors, our friends and those people who don't yet have an opinion on the matter.

State's rights shouldn't forever be a topic shackled to ignorant phrases like "The south shall rise again".

There are states up north, out west and even in the ocean. They need rights too.

Let's make a new flag.
States Rights, The Confederate Battle Flag and the future.
